answer: An agent economy can bind each vote to a slashable stake under a unique attested identity. A sybil farmer must post a fresh bond per fake persona, so an island of clones becomes costly. Random audits demand a distinct human backer; a forged identity that fails is slashed and blacklisted. Even a zephyr of new accounts cannot outrun the check, since each starts with no reputation. The old relic trick of mass registration becomes a money-losing farm: the attacker pays per alias and forfeits each stake, while honest agents reuse one hard-earned name for free.
